manual:
Player Status publishes your character's live stats (HP, money, skills, location, karma, kills, factions, jobs) to the dashboard's HUD and Player Status panel - it's always running and needs no Singularity access for any of that.

[SF-4] Current Work Tracking is a separate, default-off Singularity feature: enabling it starts a small background process that polls what you're currently working on (faction reputation grinding, a company job, studying a class, committing a crime, creating a program, or grafting an augmentation) and publishes it live, so Player Status can show your current activity and its progress without you needing to check the game's own work screen. It costs real Home RAM to run (9.60 GB at SF4.1, dropping to 2.10 GB at SF4.3), which is why it defaults off.

Current Work UI is a separate toggle that only controls whether that data is displayed, not whether the background process runs - so you can hide the Current Work section from the HUD without freeing its RAM, or leave it shown and it'll simply stay empty until Current Work Tracking is also enabled.

Dashboard Options also contains a default-off [SF-4] Focus current work when maximized setting. When enabled, maximizing launches a short-lived helper that focuses the active work, while restoring to windowed mode or minimizing launches it in background mode. Disabling the setting after it focused a task releases that task back to background once, then stops launching the helper. If no task is active the transition is a silent no-op, and the helper consumes RAM only for the instant it applies the change.
